question: In which Indian state is 'Syalde Bikhauti Mela' celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Syalde Bikhauti Mela** is a prominent annual cultural fair celebrated in the **Kumaon** region of the Indian state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• This fair takes place in the town of **Dwarahat**, located in the **Almora** district, and is held during the month of **April**, specifically coinciding with **Vishwat Sankranti** (the first day of the **Hindu** month of **Vaishakh**).
 
• The festival is divided into two distinct parts: **Syalde**, which is celebrated on the night before the main event, and **Bikhauti**, which is the primary celebration held on the day of the **Sankranti**.
 
• A unique and historical ritual of this fair is the **Oda-Bheta**, where devotees strike a particular stone with a stick to symbolize the victory over an ancient rival clan, the **Katpuria**, reflecting the region's martial history.
 
• The fair serves as a platform for the preservation of local folk traditions, featuring traditional dances like the **Jhora** and **Chanchari**, and folk songs that narrate the legends of the **Himalayan** foothills.
 
• Thousands of people from neighboring villages and tourists visit the **Shitaladevi Temple** during this period to seek blessings and participate in the vibrant festivities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Landscape of Uttarakhand:** Known as **Devbhoomi** (Land of the Gods), **Uttarakhand** is home to two primary cultural zones, **Garhwal** and **Kumaon**, each hosting a variety of fairs linked to seasonal changes and religious legends.
 
• **Major Fairs in the State:**
 
 
• **Kumbh Mela:** Held in **Haridwar** every **12 years**, it is one of the largest religious congregations in the world and is recognized by **UNESCO** as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage**.
 
• **Nanda Devi Raj Jat:** A grand pilgrimage and fair that takes place once every **12 years**, tracing a long trek through the high-altitude mountains of **Chamoli**.
 
• **Bagwal Mela:** Celebrated at the **Devidhura** temple in **Champawat** district during **Raksha Bandhan**, it is famous for its ritualistic stone-pelting tradition.
 
• **Jauljibi Mela:** An international trade and cultural fair held at the confluence of the **Kali** and **Gori** rivers, facilitating exchange between people from **India**, **Nepal**, and **Tibet**.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Importance:** These melas (fairs) are not only religious events but also serve as important trade hubs for local artisans to sell traditional **Kumaoni** and **Garhwali** crafts, woolens, and organic mountain produce.
 
• **Festivals of Uttarakhand:** Other significant festivals include **Phool Dei** (the spring flower festival), **Harela** (marking the onset of the rainy season), and **Ghee Sankranti**, all of which emphasize the state's deep connection with nature and agriculture.
